content:
Alex: quick midday handoff — TL;DR: this morning we paged on high KV cache eviction rate which caused increased upstream latency and a handful of 429s for embedding requests. most customer impact was transient; we mitigated with a soft throttle and a targeted batcher restart.

IncidentBot: Pager: `kv-cache.evictions.rate` alert triggered 2026-03-14 07:12 UTC (sev3). 13 pages. Escalation path followed.

Alex: timeline:
- 07:12 alert fired (eviction rate spike during background compaction).
- 07:20 automated throttles kicked in (reduced ingress to batchers).
- 07:28 first manual mitigation: restarted batcher group `batcher-zone-3` (rolling restart).
- 07:35 eviction rate trending down, 429s subsided, customer impact minimized.

Maria: i'm taking primary for the midday->evening block (12:00-20:00 UTC). i'm aware of a partial coverage gap 18:30-19:15 where Jong and i both have constrained availability (travel overlap). i've scheduled Ash as backup between 18:30-19:30 — @Ash please ack when you can cover that slot. :pray:

Ash: acked, i'll be on call 18:30-19:30 and reachable on phone + slack.

Jong: i'll be secondary 12:00-20:00. also owning the post-incident follow-up and short postmortem draft (ENG-5423). plan to include root cause hypothesis + recommended threshold change.

Alex: current status:
- KV eviction rate: back to baseline but still noisy during compaction windows.
- Affected endpoints: embedding ingestion (small % of requests returned 429s between 07:12-07:40).
- Customer impact: small number of retries observed for two enterprise customers (ticketed; support loop opened).
- Runbook: followed `kv-eviction` runbook steps; worked but runbook misses a quick check we needed (see action items).

SRE-Runbook-Bot: quick links:
- Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-eviction
- Playbook snippet:
```
# check eviction metrics
kubectl -n inference exec -it svc/kv-metrics -- curl localhost:9090/metrics | grep kv_cache_evictions
# restart batcher group
gcloud compute ssh batcher-zone-3 --command "sudo systemctl restart redwood-batcher"
```

Maria: notes & next steps for my shift:
- Watch compaction window at 14:00 and 20:00 UTC — increase sampling of eviction metrics during those windows.
- Temporarily lower the eviction alert threshold to reduce noisy autoscale decisions: set `evictions.rate` threshold from 50/s -> 30/s for the next 48h (monitor).
- If eviction rate spikes and 5xx/429 > 1% for >5m, run targeted batcher restart; follow runbook.
- Inform support & account teams for the two impacted customers with status update by 13:30.

Alex: action items captured:
- (Jong) own ENG-5423 postmortem draft — include timeline, batcher restart details, and proposed alert threshold change. (due EOD).
- (Maria) adjust alert threshold and watch for side effects.
- (Ash) cover 18:30-19:30 overlap and be primary for any pages during that window.
- (Alex) file infra task to add a quick check to runbook for compaction detection and batcher pre-warm (INFRA-1287).

Maria: quick checklist for next shift handover:
- confirm alert threshold reverted/kept and why.
- share any customer follow-ups in the ticket.
- confirm batcher health (rollout status, restarts count).

Jong: postmortem notes i'll include:
- root cause hypothesis: compaction + partial memory pressure caused eviction spikes in zone-3 batchers.
- mitigation worked: automated throttle + targeted restart.
- follow-ups: add compaction flag in metrics, add runbook step to pre-warm batchers, tune alert thresholds, consider adding cross-zone fallback routing during compaction windows.

Alex: closing notes — no ongoing customer degradation, on-call coverage confirmed for midday->evening. please ping in-thread if anything changes and @here if we need to page. :thumbsup:

Maria: thanks team. i'll post a short shift summary in #eng-oncall at 12:05 with links to ENG-5423 and INFRA-1287.

Jong: noted, i'll start the postmortem skeleton now and tag reviewers.

SRE-Runbook-Bot: runbook updated? If you'd like i can create a PR template for the new compaction check.

Alex: yes please, that would help. thanks all.
